newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs climb on discount to cash,pork bellies up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs climb on discount to cash,pork bellies up.

text.p: The sharp discount CME October hog futures hold compared with the CME lean hog index after August's expiration and technical demand lifted CME lean hog futures to higher closes, traders said. Firmer cash belly prices and holding of deliveries by strong hands pushed August and other pork bellies contracts higher as well, traders said.

Hog futures closed 1.100 to 0.025 cent a lb higher with October up most at 73.025 cents versus the latest CME lean hog index at 79.21 cents per lb. August expired at midday at 79.150 cents, off 0.050 on the day.
Pork bellies ended up 0.875 to 1.200 cent with August up 1.100 at 85.950 cents and February up least at 74.625 cents.
October hog's discount to the index with August off the board added to a strong technical picture in hogs.

October punched through early chart resistance at 72.500 and later resistance at 73.000 to reach one-week highs. That month had been holding a larger discount to August and the index which prompted much of the recent strength, they said.
"October looks cheap after the August expiration," one trader said.
Rand Financials and Rosenthal Collins bought October late after early demand from R.J. O'Brien and Refco, traders said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock sold December 72 calls. Volatility was soft in October and December on commission house call offerings, pit sources said.
